title: Ancient Egypt
description: Pharaohs, pyramids and the Nile: three thousand years of Egyptian civilization

questions.question: Which river was the lifeline of ancient Egyptian civilization?
questions.explanation: The Nile's yearly flood left fertile silt along its banks, making farming possible in an otherwise desert land.

questions.question: For which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid of Giza built?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was built for Khufu (also called Cheops) of the Fourth Dynasty, around 2560 BC.

questions.question: What was the name of the writing system using pictures and symbols in ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: Egyptians wrote with hieroglyphs. Cuneiform was used in Mesopotamia and Linear B in Mycenaean Greece.

questions.question: Which artifact was key to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone carries the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek. Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.

questions.question: Who discovered the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922?
questions.explanation: British archaeologist Howard Carter found the tomb in the Valley of the Kings in November 1922, with funding from Lord Carnarvon.

questions.question: Who was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra VII ruled until her death in 30 BC, after which Egypt became a Roman province.

questions.question: Which pharaoh tried to shift Egyptian worship to a single sun god, the Aten?
questions.explanation: Akhenaten promoted worship of the Aten and founded a new capital at Amarna. His reforms were reversed after his death.

questions.question: What material did Egyptians make from a reed to write on?
questions.explanation: Papyrus was made from strips of the papyrus plant pressed together. Our word 'paper' comes from it.

questions.question: Which female pharaoh ruled during the 18th Dynasty and is known for her temple at Deir el-Bahari?
questions.explanation: Hatshepsut ruled as pharaoh in the 15th century BC. Her mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari is one of Egypt's best-known monuments.

questions.question: Why did ancient Egyptians mummify their dead?
choices: To prevent the spread of disease
To preserve the body for the afterlife
questions.explanation: Egyptians believed the soul needed a preserved body to live on in the afterlife, so they embalmed and wrapped the dead.
